_comment: Canned web for the $0 run of the T3 example (tasks/examples/t3-web-report.yaml). Stand-in pages on a reserved .example domain, written for this repo; the real run searches the live web.

https://docs.fixtures.example/sqlite/lic.title: SQLite: license
body: SQLite is released into the public domain, so there is no license to buy or to comply with.
Anyone may copy, modify, publish, use, sell or distribute the code for any purpose, commercial or not.

https://notes.fixtures.example/sqlite-li.title: Notes on SQLite license
body: The SQLite source code carries no copyright claim: its authors dedicated it to the public domain.
Organizations that need a formal assurance can buy a warranty of title, which is sold separately.

https://docs.fixtures.example/sqlite/dep.title: SQLite: deployment
body: SQLite is a library that runs inside your application process, so there is no database server to install or administer.
The application reads and writes a single database file on disk.

https://notes.fixtures.example/sqlite-de.title: Notes on SQLite deployment
body: SQLite is embedded: it is linked into the program that uses it and needs no separate server process.
Several processes can open the same file, but writes are serialized.

https://docs.fixtures.example/duckdb/lic.title: DuckDB: license
body: DuckDB is released under the MIT license, a permissive open source license.
The MIT license allows commercial use, modification and redistribution as long as the copyright notice is kept.

https://notes.fixtures.example/duckdb-li.title: Notes on DuckDB license
body: The code of DuckDB is open source under the MIT license.
Extensions are distributed separately and may carry their own licenses.

https://docs.fixtures.example/duckdb/dep.title: DuckDB: deployment
body: DuckDB is an in-process analytical database: it runs inside the host application, so there is no server to set up.
It can query files such as Parquet and CSV directly from the application.

https://notes.fixtures.example/duckdb-de.title: Notes on DuckDB deployment
body: Like SQLite, DuckDB is embedded and has no separate server process.
It is designed for analytical queries on one machine rather than for many concurrent network clients.

https://docs.fixtures.example/postgresql.title: PostgreSQL: license
body: PostgreSQL is released under the PostgreSQL License, a liberal open source license similar to the BSD and MIT licenses.
The license permits use, copying, modification and distribution for any purpose, without fee.

https://notes.fixtures.example/postgresq.title: Notes on PostgreSQL license
body: The PostgreSQL License is an open source license approved by the OSI.
No single company owns the code, which is maintained by the PostgreSQL Global Development Group.

https://docs.fixtures.example/postgresql.title: PostgreSQL: deployment
body: PostgreSQL runs as a separate server process that applications reach over the network or a local socket.
Clients connect through a driver, and many sessions can be served at the same time.

https://notes.fixtures.example/postgresq.title: Notes on PostgreSQL deployment
body: PostgreSQL is a client/server database: the server is installed, configured and monitored apart from the application.
Managed hosting is offered by many cloud providers.
